N3.interpretation: Fixed-tile single-change and combined ablations versus the same algorithm's plain variant; no claim that individual gains add linearly.

N4.interpretation: Synthetic numerical characterization, including retained failures and near cancellation. Reported maxima are maxima of the saved reference-check scopes, not global certification.
N4.real_matrix_values: Not covered by synthetic v1; separate supplement remains required for the original N4 scope.

limitations: These are current fixed-tile elementary kernels and bounded tile screens, not the strongest independently tuned cubic or Strassen baselines.
N2 minima are best observed screening measurements; they are not fresh confirmations, globally optimal tiles, or a deployed selection rule.
There are no held-out generalization, v6e replication, model-quality, or end-to-end LLM performance claims in N1--N4.

Core v1 LLM-associated shapes use synthetic BF16 matrices. The optional separately reported real-weight supplement uses actual weight tensors with synthetic activations; it does not test real activation distributions or model quality.
Complete-call timing includes device preparation/padding and output cropping; it excludes compilation and host transfers. Prepared-kernel results remain separate in the evidence.
A confidence interval containing one is inconclusive at this measurement precision; it does not establish equal performance. Intervals are per-comparison, without familywise multiplicity correction.
Sampled-reference errors cover a saved row-column cross-product using all K, not a certified maximum over the complete output. Whole-output finite checks are separate.
Machine identity describes one logical allocation/runtime and exposed device attributes, not an independently verified permanent physical-chip serial number.

n4_real_weight_supplement.interpretation: Actual BF16 Qwen3-0.6B layer-0 q_proj/down_proj weights with synthetic Gaussian A; B is weight.T. Four plain algorithms, M=512/2048, three seeds: 48 numerical cases.
n4_real_weight_supplement.real_matrix_values: Actual weight tensors only; activations remain synthetic. This is separate from the 480-case synthetic core v1 N4 cohort.

N4.purpose: Supplement the 480 core synthetic numerical cases with 48 separately identified real-weight cases, retaining identical numerical gates.

real_weights.provenance: Require pinned 40-hex checkpoint revision, config/license hashes, raw tensor hashes, shapes, BF16 dtype, and little-endian byte layout. Save verified manifest and transpose hashes in every run.

config_snapshot/campaign_real_weights_v1.inheritance: Retain base v1 device, precision, correctness gates, memory limits and immutable execution policy; override only the fields explicitly present here. The effective campaign is saved in each run.

input_semantics.a: Synthetic Gaussian activation-shaped matrix: PCG64(seed).standard_normal((M,K), dtype=float32) / float32(sqrt(K)), then quantize once to BF16.
input_semantics.b: Actual layer-0 checkpoint weight transposed from [output,input] to [K,N]; verified stored BF16 values are preserved exactly.
input_semantics.scope: Real-weight matrix multiplication accuracy; not real activations, model output quality, or end-to-end inference.
input_semantics.seed_reuse: A depends only on its shape and the specified seed. All arms consume the identical A and B. The independent reference uses these exact quantized operands.

config_snapshot/shapes_real_weights_v1.j.input_semantics: B is an actual checkpoint weight transpose; A remains synthetic Gaussian BF16.

weights_provenance.json.scope: Actual public checkpoint weights only. No activations downloaded; any synthetic activations must be labeled separately. No model-quality result is implied.
